dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of Wednesday 25 November 2026 on contracts drafted by the GitHub Actions fetch job from Tuesday 24 November's close, which had already landed when this session started - no wait was needed. Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-24. What was excluded, and it matters more than usual this session: the four news-log entries dated 25 November, which cover the 8:30am release of October PCE and the Q3 GDP second estimate - the single print every Macro calendar vote in this document is written around. Those votes describe the risk as it stood at Tuesday's close, with consensus figures taken from sources dated 23-24 November, and nothing from the actual release influenced a vote or a number. Also excluded: anything dated 25 November on the tariff proposal and chip rout that the 25 November news-log entries record.

The session was a rotation, not a liquidation, and that is the fact most of this document turns on. The S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 (ES=F -0.93%) for its eighth loss in nine sessions and the Nasdaq-100 cash index fell 1.99% (NQ=F -2.35%), while the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, the Russell 2000 rose 0.57%, equal-weight RSP rose 0.54%, breadth ran 346 advancers to 154 decliners and nine of eleven sectors were higher. The whole decline sat in one industry: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -7.88%, SOXX -8.27%, Technology the only sector below -1% at -3.26%. The VIX barely moved, -0.98% to 26.36, and credit tightened for the first time in this document's recent window - high-yield spreads 356bp (-11bp), investment grade 94bp (-2bp). That combination is why the S&P 500 resolves bullish at all three horizons on mostly non-price categories while the Nasdaq-100 resolves flat at one and five sessions.

This document carries the first non-zero volRegime-or-crowd value in the ledger's record: crowd is -1 for the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq-100, and 0 for the other four. The change is in the sourcing, not in judgment. Earlier boards set crowd to 0 because the Goldman desk figures then available carried no percentile; the figures now available do. Two independent reports of the same Goldman Sachs prime-brokerage briefing dated 23 November themselves name fundamental long/short net leverage of 42.3% at the 1st percentile of the past year on one account and the 5th percentile of one year and 3rd of three years on another, beta-adjusted net exposure at a 1st-percentile three-year reading described elsewhere as a five-year low, the largest weekly single-stock shorting flow since June 2022, and - for the Nasdaq-100 specifically - CTA positioning 'near the bottom of its 10-year range'. The value is set at -1 rather than the -2 the cap allows because the readings are one session old, reached through secondary reporting, and the two accounts disagree on the exact percentile. It changes no call in this document: the S&P 500's three cells are bullish and so read as opposing a negative stretch, and the Nasdaq-100's three resolve to flat or no-call, which the overlay leaves alone. It does change two reported stretch labels - the S&P 500 from neutral to stretched-down at -2, the Nasdaq-100 from stretched-down to extreme-down at -3 - and that is recorded here so the change is visible rather than silent.

Sigma inputs: one improved, two are still carried, and all three are documented in their sigmaSource fields with the direction of the error stated. The dollar's is dated on S for the first time in this ledger - EUR/USD one-month at-the-money implied volatility of 6.35% as of 24 November from FinanceFeeds' options tables - replacing the 6.10% 13 November reading the last three boards carried; the components are identical at either value, so the +4 does not rest on the switch. The Russell's RVX is now carried two sessions from 20 November's 36.88 because no 23 or 24 November value was obtainable, and with the VIX at 26.36 that very likely overstates small-cap volatility and widens the Russell's bands - but the stretch label is 0 at 36.88 and -1 at a sigma of 27, both neutral. Bonds' TLT implied-volatility carry of 15 is now 41 sessions stale and remains the one input here that is clearly wrong in level rather than merely old; MOVE's latest dated print is 106.31 from 20 November and cannot be converted into a ZN=F percentage sigma without inventing a conversion, so the carry stands and the distortion - narrow Treasury bands, 1D 0.47% - is recorded rather than fixed. Two further gauges came up one session short in the fetch itself: no GVZ and no VXN value dated 24 November was returned, so gold's sigma is 23 November's 31.25 and the Nasdaq-100's is 23 November's 36.31. In both cases a gauge that rose with the day's decline would make the stretch reading shallower, not deeper, so neither carry manufactures its asset's score.

The 10-session horizon now matures on 9 December, the second day of the FOMC meeting, so for the first time in this ledger the decision itself falls inside a live window rather than one session past it. Every 10-session Fed path vote here is written on that basis, with a 25bp hike priced at about 94-96% across CME FedWatch, Polymarket and Kalshi on S - down from roughly 98% on Monday - and Kitco at about 95%. The 1-session horizon matures 25 November, which puts October PCE, the Q3 GDP second estimate, October durable goods, jobless claims and the Beige Book inside a single-day window.

Gold's stretch reading is the deepest in this ledger's record: -5, with all four price-based components firing at once for the first time for this asset. The 2.97% session took RSI back under 30 to 29.62 and put the close 0.95% above the 252-session closing low of 3515.40, inside the range component's 2% trigger, on top of a z50 of -6.63 and a z200 of -10.11. It is one of exactly two cells the overlay changes here; the other is the dollar's 5-session bullish call, which rides a +4 extreme-up reading at margin 5 and is dampened from solid to lean the same way. Neither direction is altered - the overlay cannot flip one - and no cell was vetoed to flat this session, since no continuation call into an extreme landed on the margin-4 threshold.

Bonds' 1-session horizon is live for the first time in four boards, and the reason is mechanical rather than new evidence: the computed hourly structure read turned to uptrend, and category 13's mechanical vote carries weight 3, which on its own lifts the weighted live count past the gate of 7. The 5- and 10-session horizons remain below the gate and resolve to no-call, as they have on every board since 20 November, because this asset still has no dated positioning figure, sentiment survey, breadth analogue, earnings analogue or seasonality statistic available for the window.

newsLog.event: Sanofi agreed to acquire respiratory-disease specialist Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion, the largest pharma acquisition in three years. The deal brings Sanofi Brinsupri (brensocatib), Arikayce and the phase 3 TPIP program as it faces the loss of patent protection on its top-selling drug; Sanofi said its 2026 financial guidance is unaffected.
newsLog.numbers: $175/share cash, $41.0B / EUR37.6B total; ~46% premium to Insmed's Nov 18 close (the day before Bloomberg reported Sanofi was weighing a bid); INSM +14% premarket, Sanofi shares +4.7% to EUR89.38, a one-year high. Largest industry deal since Pfizer-Seagen ($43B, Dec 2023)
newsLog.reaction: Insmed rallied toward the offer and Sanofi rose on the strategic fix for its patent cliff; the size of the deal revives large-cap pharma M&A expectations and gives biotech a bid on an otherwise soft tape.
